insights.statement: Net new ARR fell €5.6M (from €10.4M to €4.8M) and higher churn explains 80.4% of the fall: churned ARR rose €4.5M (from 3.3 to 7.8) while new-logo ARR rose €0.2M
insights.decision_relevance: The slowdown is a retention problem; a sales-hiring answer targets the part of the bridge that did not break

insights.statement: Expansion ARR fell €1.3M (from 4.3 to 3.0), the second leak in the bridge; new and expansion together barely moved while churn more than doubled
insights.decision_relevance: Expansion recovery is a second lever, owned by customer success, not by new AEs
insights.caveat: No source explains the expansion decline directly (H6 unresolved)

insights.statement: The sales engine did not break: pipeline created grew 18.0% (€38.9M to €45.9M), deals won rose from 175 to 193 and win rate held at 23% to 24%
insights.decision_relevance: There is no evidence that a lack of sellers capped 2025 growth, so 30 extra AEs are not the obvious fix

insights.statement: Price pressure is real but marginal: average new ARR per deal slipped from €53.7k to €49.7k and price is cited in 34% of lost deals, yet only 31% of churned customers cite a competitor or price
insights.decision_relevance: Pricing deserves monitoring, not the 2026 budget

insights.statement: The leak is concentrated in new customers: customers onboarded in the previous 12 months churned 26% in 2025 versus 12% in 2024 (+14 pp), and supplied 60.3% of churned ARR (€4.7M of €7.8M) while mature customers churned 9%
insights.decision_relevance: Fixing the first year of the customer life is where the money is

insights.statement: The first-year churn spike follows the February 2025 onboarding cut that saved €0.8M a year: median time to first value rose from 21 to 48 days and 58% of churned customers say they never fully implemented; excess first-year churn above the 2024 rate cost €2.5M of ARR
insights.decision_relevance: A €0.8M saving cost about €2.5M of ARR; reversing it is the highest-return use of the 2026 budget
insights.caveat: Causality inferred from timing and exit interviews, not from a controlled test

insights.statement: The CRO's €9M equals 30 AEs at full €300k productivity for a whole year; with a 9-month ramp, Q1 hires deliver at most €4.5M in 2026, a €4.5M shortfall, for €3.6M a year
insights.decision_relevance: The plan as proposed does not hold; the board would be buying half the promised ARR, and new customers would flow into an onboarding team that cannot retain them
insights.caveat: €4.5M is an upper bound that relies on assumption A001 (linear ramp from a mid-Q1 start)

insights.statement: A retention-first plan costs €2.0M a year (restore onboarding for €0.8M plus 10 AEs for €1.2M), frees €1.6M versus the CRO plan, and identifies up to €5.3M of the €5.6M needed to restore 2024 net new ARR
insights.decision_relevance: This is the approvable alternative: more ARR per euro, with hiring wave 2 released only when retention is fixed
insights.caveat: All three levers are upper bounds to validate (A001, A002, H6)
